title: A row action's requiredPermissions is inert inside a record page's related list — same declaration gates correctly on record_header
body:
## Summary

A row action that declares `requiredPermissions` is **not** gated inside a record page's related-list panel: it renders for a caller whose reported capability set is `[]`. The same action, same declaration, same build, **is** correctly hidden on the record surface (`record_header`). So the capability reaches one evaluator and not the other.

Measured on objectui `efead6c6` (the pin objectstack-ai/cloud declares), framework `6ff5b562`, against a real control plane with a real org owner and a real plain member.

## Reading

Action: `sys_domain.set_primary`, declared `locations: ['list_item', 'record_header']` + `requiredPermissions: ['manage_org_users']`.

Reported capabilities (`GET /api/v1/auth/me/permissions`):

```
owner  → systemPermissions: ["manage_org_users", "setup.access", "setup.write"]
member → systemPermissions: []          // reported EMPTY, not absent
```

Same build, same viewport (1440×900), two surfaces:

| surface | owner | plain member | expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| `record_header` (the domain record page) | shown | **hidden** | ✅ matches |
| `list_item` (the related-list panel on the environment record page) | shown | **shown** | ❌ should be hidden |

## Where it comes from

`packages/react/src/hooks/useCapabilityGate.ts` is explicit that unknown fails open:

> Source of truth … the ActionProvider's runner context (`user.systemPermissions`) … with the ambient predicate scope as fallback … **Fail-OPEN when unknown.** No runner, no user, no `systemPermissions` array: the action shows. … An EMPTY array is not unknown — it means "holds nothing" and gates normally.

The member's set is `[]`, i.e. the "gates normally" case. It gates normally on the record surface and not in the related-list rows, so on that mount `useHeldCapabilities()` must be resolving to `undefined` — the panel's action runtime does not carry `systemPermissions` into the runner context (nor into the predicate scope it publishes), and the deliberate fail-open then shows a button the server refuses with 403.

The fail-open doctrine itself is not in question — hiding a permitted user's button on missing client data is the worse failure. What is wrong is that the data **is** available on this page (the record surface one level up gates correctly off it) and simply is not threaded into the panel's runtime.

## Why it matters downstream

objectstack-ai/cloud#2224: a plain organization member was offered Set as Primary / Verify DNS / Delete on an environment's domain rows and read a red 403 toast on click. The maintainer ruled the buttons must be hidden; cloud moved the permission term onto `requiredPermissions` (the key the framework spec names for exactly this, beside `visible`'s "these are not access control" note). It lands on the record surface and is inert in the rows — which is the surface the users actually hit.

## Repro

Any object whose action declares both locations plus a `requiredPermissions` the caller lacks; render it once on its own record page and once as a related list inside the parent's record page, with a session whose `/auth/me/permissions` reports `systemPermissions: []`.

Related: objectui#4421 (object-level `can()`; and the record-level gap I described in its comments). This card is narrower and does not need a new binding — the value is already fetched on the page.
